segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hey Dana, sorry I'm five minutes behind. I had the renewal screen open from the ops cleanup and lost track. You still good for a quick pricing pass?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yeah, ten minutes is fine. We’re looking at 72 seats to start, with maybe another 15 after the March hiring class.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. For 72 seats, annual subscription is $38,880, and the one-time onboarding package is $6,500. If you add the 15 later, they’d prorate into the same term.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Finance asked if we can do quarterly invoices instead of all upfront. Net 30, same as the pilot.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, quarterly invoicing and net 30 both work. The term would run February 1 through January 31, unless you want the go-live date to drive it.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: We’re targeting go-live on January 22. I don’t want to pay for three weeks where nobody’s using it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Totally fair. We can set the billing start at January 22. The only thing is your account has two billing addresses in the CRM, so I’m going to fix that before I generate the quote or the tax line can come out weird.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Use the Omaha address. The Denver office is just a receiving site, no invoices there.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. Standard 12-month term, quarterly invoices, 72 seats at launch, Omaha billing. I can get the order form over by 4:30; I just need to paste the approved discount into the internal cover sheet first so it routes cleanly.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Send it to me and copy Marcus in procurement. If the numbers match what you said, we should be able to sign by Friday.
